summary: Passes: the round 1 gap is closed (the road has a destination from frame 0 and line 3 now runs on into line 4), so something is pending from the first frame to the last; what remains is that the payoff's second row can be read 1.8 s before it is spoken, and that the rests between lines still depend on the drawing moving.

must: line 3 an unfinished clause that line 4 completes
round_1_fixes.made: yes, with other wording than mine, which the fix allowed: "Until one word," / "the light stays on."; pause 1.4 s; three road dots for three words; 32 words; run 24.38 s; turn starts at 54%

round_1_fixes.made: 'light' yes (1.6 s) and 'fine' unchanged. The payoff rest was not cut to 1.5 s: review.md ruling 1 overrode it (payoff spoken over two beats with a 0.6 s pause, then a 1.8 s breath with the drawing moving). I accept the ruling and judge the result as written

Checked again on the new vo.wav: transcribe.py puts the eight spoken beats' first words at 1.46, 4.08, 7.46, 9.90, 12.72, 16.11, 17.81 and 20.23 s against vo_start 1.45, 4.605, 7.796, 10.443, 13.262, 16.343, 18.056 and 20.611 s (0.23 to 0.54 s early on seven of eight), so the rule is needed; every word between first and last falls inside its own beat, so the rule as written works on this track

findings.ours: No beat can now be deleted with nothing lost. 'until' (7.80 to 9.04 s, "Until one word,") was the deletable line in round 1 as "One word will do."; it is now half a sentence, and it plants the one word the last frame answers. 'light' (10.44 to 11.66 s) completes it and lights the window. 'again' (4.61 to 6.20 s) still adds no words: it is the refrain's immediate repeat and stays for that reason only. The payoff's two beats ('asking' 16.34 to 17.46 s, 'love' 18.06 to 18.81 s) are one line, not a repeat.
findings.reference: barsat-song 13.4 to 16.5 s and 16.8 to 20.2 s: first line repeated at once. 20.2 to 22.8 s: line 3 is an unfinished clause that line 4 (23.7 s) completes; ours now does the same at 7.80 and 10.44 s.
findings.why_it_matters: The first new line after the repeat now pulls forward instead of resting.

findings.criterion: an open question at every moment
findings.ours: By stretch: 0.00 to 22.2 s, the road is heading for a window that is on the sheet, unlit, from frame 0 (does it arrive). 7.80 to 11.66 s, an unfinished sentence. 7.80 to about 22.8 s, which word (answered only by "Home." in the last frame). 13.26 to 18.81 s, "I know you're fine." opens then why ask. 18.81 to 22.2 s, the gap between road and window closing. The thin stretch is 2.96 to 7.80 s (4.8 s, 20% of the run, down from 8.2 s and 35%): nothing is pending in the words there, 'again' is a verbatim repeat, and the only thread is the picture one. It holds only if a square of "a few sparse dots" reads as a window, and as where the road is going, before it lights at 10.5 s. The script's own stated question (why keep asking) still opens in words only at 13.26 s, 54%.
findings.reference: barsat-song 13.4 s: the first sung line is a plea with an unknown outcome, held to about 73 to 77 s, 0.40 of its run (tentative, per the breakdown), so its question is open in words from the first line. Ours is open in the picture from the first frame and in words from 7.80 s (32%).
findings.why_it_matters: From 3 to 8 s the hold rests on one small drawn thing. If it does not read at phone size, round 1's gap is back at a little over half its length.

findings.ours: 40% to 70% of the run is 9.75 to 17.06 s. In it: "the light stays on." completes the sentence and the window lights with one added layer in the sound (10.44 to 11.66 s, 43% to 48%); the turn "I know you're fine." (13.26 to 14.24 s, 54% to 58%, earlier than round 1's 61%) removes worry as the reason and changes how the refrain reads; the first half of the payoff starts at 16.34 s (67%). The longest rest of the run, 2.18 s audible silence at 14.18 to 16.36 s, sits here, but it follows the turn, so "then why ask" covers it and the road is drawn running straight at the window through it.
findings.reference: barsat-song 69.3 to 89.7 s (0.37 to 0.48 of its run): a block of new verse lines in which its question appears to be answered; refrain back at 0.49 to 0.58. Ours puts new lines and its turn in the same part of the run.
findings.why_it_matters: The turn is what makes the payoff more than the answer the viewer assumed at 3 s. It is in the right place and should not move later.

findings.ours: 32 words in 24.38 s (79 a minute; word budget 24 to 32, met). Line starts are 3.16, 3.19, 2.65, 2.82 and 3.08 s apart, then 4.27 s for the payoff line; no cut. Two things are short of the yardstick. (a) Rests. Measured on vo.wav, the audible silences between lines are 1.73, 1.68, 1.48, 1.68, 2.18 and 1.88 s, plus 0.68 s inside the payoff line and 2.24 s at the end; the voice is audible for about 42% of the run. Each rest now has something pending and the script puts dots on the sheet in every one, so this is no longer a script fault, but it is the script's largest dependency on the producer. (b) Picture ahead of voice on the one line where it costs. Under the sync rule a line appears whole in faint ink at the start of its slot. For six lines that is 0.12 s before the voice. For the payoff line it puts row two, "I love you.", on the sheet at 16.22 s and the voice reaches it at 18.06 s: the answer can be read 1.83 s before it is said, and before the voice has finished the word "Asking". The 0.6 s pause that ruling 1 added then withholds nothing from anyone who reads.
findings.reference: barsat-song lyric_lines: line slot 3.0 to 4.1 s (ours 2.65 to 4.27 s; the two short ones are one sentence over 5.5 s); longest gap between lines 1.2 s (all six of ours are longer, by 0.3 to 1.0 s); voiced part of slot 2.3 to 3.7 s (ours 0.75 to 1.6 s). The benchmarks' notes expect a spoken line to be shorter than its slot and leave the fill to the producer. For when a lyric row should appear relative to the voice the reference gives nothing (lyrics_on_screen.caption_lead_or_lag_s is null), so (b) is held to the brief only and cannot be a must.
findings.why_it_matters: The split delivery exists to put time on the peak. If the eye has the answer at 67% of the run, the 1.8 s that follow are the voice catching up with something already known, in the part of the run where a viewer who has the answer leaves.

findings.ours: Seven lines of 3 to 6 words, one idea each, all to "you", no name, number or term to introduce; one line at a time in one fixed place; rows break as phrases ("I know" / "you're fine.", "Asking is how" / "I love you."). One line leans on the screen: "Until one word," is elliptical (until one word comes) and is not a sentence by itself. I cannot hear the track; measured on vo.wav, the voice ends "word," at about 99 to 101 Hz, the same floor it ends full sentences on (97 to 113 Hz), and I synthesised the unsplit sentence "Until one word, the light stays on." with the same voice and pace and it falls to the same floor at the comma. So the ear probably gets a closed fall, then 1.48 s of silence, then "the light stays on."; the comma and the lower-case "the" on screen are what say the sentence is still running. Merging lines 3 and 4 into one beat would not change that. "Asking is how" ends the same way (about 100 Hz), as script.md already says; there the unsplit line does hold the pitch up (about 175 to 185 Hz on "how").
findings.reference: barsat-song 13.4 to 107.5 s: lines of 3 to 6 words, most often 4 (ours the same). The reference shows no lyric on screen and is sung, so there is nothing to hold the row setting or the spoken intonation to.
findings.why_it_matters: No line needs hearing twice if the comma is seen. A viewer who only listens may take line 3 as a stray fragment for a second and a half.

findings.ours: "Asking is how / I love you." (16.34 to 18.81 s, 67% to 77% of the run; "I love you." 74% to 77%) answers the script's question in full, is the longest line and has the longest slot (4.27 s). It is told in words and then shown: the road's last stretch starts closing about 0.6 s after "you" and reaches the sill on the final "home" at about 22.0 s. The one weakness is when the eye gets it, which is the pace finding above.
findings.reference: No firm reference: benchmarks pacing.payoff_at_share_of_run is null. Tentatively barsat-song answers at about 0.40 and keeps returning to the refrain; its long lines addressed straight to the other person are at 168.0 to 182.9 s (0.91 to 0.99), with about twice the usual slot. Ours gives its direct line 1.3 to 1.6 times the other slots and the refrain after it.
findings.why_it_matters: It lands because of the turn before it; both are in place.

findings.ours: The run continues 5.56 s after the payoff ends (18.81 to 24.38 s, 23% of the run; round 1 was 4.75 s, 20%). It is longer but every part now carries something new: 18.81 to 19.4 s the lit line holds (0.6 s, still); 19.4 to 20.61 s the gap to the window is seen closing; 20.61 to 22.20 s the refrain returns with a changed meaning, the last dot reaches the sill and "home" turns red as it is spoken; 22.20 to 22.8 s the ink words fade; at about 22.8 s the red word resets to "Home.", which answers "which word" from 7.80 s; then 1.6 s to read it, with the bed sounding and dots gathering. The last frame sits where the first frame's red word sat, so a loop restarts cleanly. Two limits: 1.6 s is the most this hold can carry, and the reset is a small change (one capital, one full stop) that has to be seen as an event or the last 2.2 s read as a still.
findings.reference: barsat-song 182.9 to 185.33 s: the same card for 2.4 to 3.0 s after the last word, the last 1.72 s silent (a Do not copy). Ours runs 2.18 s after the last word with one change at about 0.6 s and no silence.
findings.why_it_matters: The final 2.2 s are the last 9% of the run; a viewer who swipes there is counted as not finishing.

fixes.change: Do not put the payoff's second row on the sheet before the voice gets near it. In beat 'asking', change the picture and motion so that only row one, "Asking is how", is on the sheet from the start of the beat (faint, then lit word by word), with the space under it empty. Row two, "I love you.", arrives in faint ink at that beat's vo_end (17.46 s in the current timing.json), at the start of the 0.6 s pause, and lights from beat 'love' vo_start as now. Row one stays in place, so the line is still kept on screen as ruling 1 requires, and a muted viewer still reads row two 0.6 s ahead of the voice. Add the exception to carries_through.sync_rule: "Line 6 is the one line that does not appear whole: its second row arrives at the pause." No change to vo, pauses or timing. If the by-ear check in script.md ends in the one-beat fallback ("Asking is how I love you." unsplit), this fix lapses: that line is then spoken within about 1.6 s of appearing, like the others.

Add "Until one word," to the To check by ear list in script.md, next to "Asking is how": measured, it ends on the same falling pitch as a full sentence (about 100 Hz) and is followed by 1.48 s without voice. Speaking lines 3 and 4 as one beat does not fix it (the voice falls at the comma there too), so do not merge them. If by ear it sounds like a closed statement followed by a gap, set pause_after_s on beat 'until' to 1.0 (from 1.4) and re-run voice.py, so the two halves sit close enough to be heard as one sentence; the run stays inside 20 to 30 s (about 24.0 s) and the turn still starts near 54%.

Show frame 0 at phone size and test one thing on it: does the unlit window read as a window, and as the place the road is going, with no words to help. Draw it as a closed square outline of dots with a cross-bar, not a loose scatter, at the height the road's first three dots point to. From 3 to 8 s it is the only thing the viewer is waiting on.

Two checks on the first cut. (1) In measure.json's timeline, no stretch without visible motion longer than about 1.2 s (the reference's longest gap between lines). The two 0.6 s holds the script asks for (road and line still after "how" and after "you") are inside that limit. The rests at 14.2 to 16.4 s and 18.8 to 20.6 s are the ones to look at. (2) The change from "home" to "Home." at about 22.8 s must be visible as an event at phone size: redraw the whole word in place over a few frames, do not swap one letter and add a dot inside a single frame.

evidence: One reference. It has public numbers (1,938,059 views, 5,421 likes, 89 comments, a 700-follower channel, as of 2026-11-25) but one video gives no result evidence: these are what the reference does, not proof of what performs. The reference is NOT a lyric video: it is one still title card held for 185.33 s under a full song, with no lyric on screen at any time, no motion and no cut. Every value about how lyrics are set, timed, moved or coloured is therefore null, and the brief governs those. Tool figures are given as measured; ranged values are the single reference's figure widened about 15% either way; length follows the brief (20 to 30 s), not the reference (185.33 s). Sung-word figures rest on a low-trust transcript of singing over a band. Beyond benchmarks.json: beat times are from 03-script/timing/timing.json (made by voice.py, so measured, not estimated from word counts). Pace was held to benchmarks lyric_lines, not to pacing.words_per_minute, as its notes direct. On 03-script/timing/vo.wav I measured the audible silences (ffmpeg silencedetect at -40 dB), ran transcribe.py to test the sync rule, and estimated the pitch at the end of each spoken beat by autocorrelation; I also synthesised four test phrases with the same voice and pace to compare split and unsplit lines. None of those working files was saved to the run folder. I cannot hear the track: the pitch figures say where the voice falls, not how it sounds. All of this is an estimate of where a viewer might leave, made against one reference that is not a lyric video; it is not a prediction of results.
